newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET - Hussain eyes part two of tour ambition.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET - Hussain eyes part two of tour ambition.

text.p: PALMERSTON NORTH, Jan 16 - Talented England batsman Nasser Hussain has achieved part one of his ambition on the twin tours of Zimbabwe and New Zealand.
He hit his third test hundred of 1996 in the first test against Zimbabwe at Bulawayo in December.
Now he is after another ton against the Kiwis, NZPA reports.
"When I left home I set my stall out to get a test 100 in Zimbabwe and another in New Zealand.
"Now I've got three tests to get that 100 against New Zealand," 28-year-old Hussain said last night.
He showed he is in good touch with 139 against the New Zealand Selection 11 yesterday, when he overcame a sluggish start to produce some entertaining strokeplay in his 229-ball innings.
That helped carry England to 427 for eight declared, and the Selection 11 were 25 for one at stumps last night, trailing by 264 runs overall going into the final day.
Hussain has had a chequered England career.
He came into the senior side for their 1990 tour of the West Indies but broke a wrist playing tennis.
He played against Australia in 1993 but was then overlooked -- in between injury problems -- until the twin home series in 1996.
Hussain hit 128 in the first test against India, 107 not out in the third, and followed up with 113 in the first test against Zimbabwe in Bulawayo.

In 1996 he scored 559 test runs at an average 50.82 to be fourth top runmaker in all tests, behind team mate -- and fellow centurion yesterday -- Alec Stewart (793 runs at 61.0) Pakistani opener Saeed Anwar (701 at 63.73) and Indian captain Sachin Tendulkar (623 at 41.53).
With the first test against New Zealand eight days away, it was ideal timing for Hussain to make a big score.
But he admitted he was in a good frame of mind before yesterday anyway.
"1996 was a good year for me so my mind didn't need much settling," he said.
"Any time you get 100 the week before a test has got to be good and I'm keen to make this year a good year."
Hussain represented England Schools and Combined Universities with captain Mike Atherton. That universities team reached the one-day Benson and Hedges Cup quarterfinals in a celebrated performance.
The pair are good friends and Hussain was emphatic last night in his assessment of Atherton's celebrated batting woes which have produced just 203 runs in 15 innings on this tour.
"It's blatantly clear the boys are 100 per cent behind him.
"He's a class player, a top captain and none of the boys would be surprised if he goes out and gets 100 at Auckland in the first test."
Hussain is sure England will acquit themselves well during the test series and said his team mates are "quietly confident" of their prospects.
He believed the New Zealand players wouldn't take much notice of England's disastrous one-day form in Zimbabwe.
"I think they're probably more surprised at some of the results towards the end of the Zimbabwe tour.
"People like Chris Cairns have been in England and seen how we play.
"He must tell the rest of them that we are a team of decent cricketers and the end of Zimbabwe might have been a bit of a blimp."
